notes:
Independent Part A critic review. Verdict fail: all 24 weather frames need revision; all seven references pass. Weather PNGs were not edited. No commit, push or branch change was made.

Visual inspection: every delivered weather PNG and reference at native 1x and nearest-neighbour 4x; all 24 frames in literal 3x3 repeats over all seven references at native scale; 3x close-ups across both wrap joins for every frame/reference combination; neutral 3x3 repeats and 8x close-ups to expose particle structure and periodicity. Evidence is in critic-r16A-1-repeat-*, critic-r16A-1-repeats-*, critic-r16A-1-junctions-*-3x.png and critic-r16A-1-particles.png. The reference background itself repeats at 288px; its road/crop boundaries are not weather seams.

Playback limitation: the browser access host was unavailable, so real-time GIF playback and perceived motion smoothness were not verified. All six existing r16-A-<name>.gif files were decoded: four distinct frames, infinite-loop metadata, 110ms/frame except snow at 160ms. Each GIF frame was matched against the corresponding final PNG over all seven references, confirming f0/f1/f2/f3 order. Quantization mean RGB error is about 1.79-2.34/255. The visual pattern/shape defects already independently require failure; mathematical loop closure is not being claimed as proof of perceptual smoothness.

Independent technical checks pass: all 24 weather files are 192x192 RGBA, contain only 2-5 nontransparent RGBA entries, use a small set of fixed alpha levels rather than antialias ramps, and have zero RGB under transparency. Coverage is below every applicable cap. Replayed every final PNG from the recorded drawn particles and positions and verified the fifth state equals f0. No boundary discontinuity was found. The 24 native/4x file sheets and 168 native reference-repeat proofs were checked against the current output pixels. All 24 output SHA-256 hashes still equal the hashes read at the start.

Positive visual findings: heavy rain is clearly darker/longer/denser than rain; snow remains visible on the winter reference; compact hail pellets have a harder grey facet; the small palettes and native square pixels are consistent; no magenta fringe or soft alpha ramp was found. Roads and settlements remain distinguishable in all seven contexts. These do not override visible periodic patterns, missing marks or incorrect sandstorm form.

Reference measurement: 48px drawn cell pitch. Independent farmland-3 match at render coordinate (672,240) gives mean RGB error 0.9057 at 48px, compared with 8.7032 at 47px and 9.4955 at 49px. Five references exactly match their recorded 288x288 camera crops. Desert exactly replays beach-base plus dunes props 0/3/4/2 at native cell coordinates; snow exactly replays grass@winter-base plus its recorded winter trees/details. No new grounds or seasonal prop partners are Part A deliverables, so summer/winter silhouette equality tests are not applicable to the weather PNGs. Existing donor art was inspected in context and not re-authored.

Native per-frame offsets (right/down positive, including the mathematical f3-to-f0 step): rain (1,6), (2,8), (1,8), (2,12); heavy_rain (2,12), (3,16), (2,16), (3,12); snow (1,2), (-1,3), (1,4), (0,3); hail (0,12), (0,16), (0,24); blizzard (8,1), (12,1), (16,2), (8,-1); sandstorm (48,0). Straight copies spaced at four times these offsets explain much of the visible regularity. Preserve seamless continuation while revising placement/drawings.
